races.name: Ocean Scotland Outdoor Advertising Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bea Kindly
runners_data.note: Consistent back-end finisher for Tracy Waggott who has placed zero wins from three runs on similar Good ground, and at 66 days since last run fitness is a legitimate query; her natural game is a deep hold-up run but with four rivals all wanting the same ground, finding clear daylight on a tight Musselburgh track looks harder than usual here.

runners_data.name: Claret And Blues
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's yard are 4/44 over 14 days which is a reasonable strike rate, and this horse's third-place at 5f on Standard at Southwell shows it can get competitive — comes here fresh off a 14-day turnaround and is one of the few in this field without a redistribution tag, so its hold-up role is genuine rather than forced.

runners_data.name: Enemy Action
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears sends Harry Russell north on this two-year-old who posted a third on Good at 5f last time — the best recent piece of form in the field relative to the hold-up cluster — and sim-going figures of 2 from 3 on Good-ish surfaces give reasonable confidence; its finishing effort will depend entirely on whether the pace is genuine enough to pull it through from off the bridle.

runners_data.name: Lairy Mary
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly is the race's sole pace-setter and has already won over 5f on Good ground, making her course-and-distance profile the standout; off just 13 days and shouldering 134lbs, her chance hinges on whether a lone uncontested lead at a comfortable pace lets her preserve enough energy to hold the closers late — the style-fit tag reflects that she is being asked to perform as a front-runner in an era where she has also shown variation.

runners_data.name: Mr Darling
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart has gone winless from five runners over the past 14 days, and this colt's form reads 0-6-6-6 at 5-6f on Good, which gives little encouragement regardless of race shape; he is a true hold-up horse shunted into a midfield mapping purely because of the field's composition, and his lowly OR of 46 makes him the longest of long shots even in the most favourable scenario.

runners_data.name: Stripes Of Glory
runners_data.note: David Allan takes the ride for Tim Easterby — the same yard that saddles the pace-setter — and this filly steps back from a 66-day break with form figures of 6-7-12 suggesting she has struggled to land a blow; she is at heart a hold-up type who has been placed into a midfield position on the map by default, and finding competitive improvement after two months off is the key unlock for any each-way interest.

races.paceDynamic: Lairy Mary is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f nursery and should lead from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Musselburgh, setting a sustainable rather than suicidal gallop with no genuine rival willing to challenge for the front. The rest of the field — Bea Kindly, Claret And Blues, Enemy Action, Mr Darling, and Stripes Of Glory — are all hold-up or rear-positioned types, meaning Lairy Mary can control tempo, dictate the fractions, and force rivals into a flat-footed chase from off the pace. With one clean leader and a field of closers unable to pressurise early, the race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: a horse that can sit just behind Lairy Mary on the bridle, or Lairy Mary herself if she finds enough, will be ideally placed when the sprint home begins. Three runners — Stripes Of Glory, Bea Kindly, and Mr Darling — are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field simply has no room for that many deep closers; of the three, Stripes Of Glory with the David Allan booking for Tim Easterby (who also trains the pace-setter) is most likely to secure a workable position, but none can be confident of getting their natural role in a race this small.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lairy Mary Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lairy Mary breaks cleanly and no rival applies early pressure, allowing her to set a relaxed, controlled tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard of the 5f, conserving energy through the early stages and arriving at the two-furlong pole with a significant positional advantage on a field of closers stuck in each other's pockets. On Good to Firm going where she has won before, and with no pace rival to stretch her, this shape heavily rewards the front-runner and any horse able to track her in second.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lairy Mary's controlled pace is still fast enough to flatten rivals, allowing one genuine closer to pick them all off with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A steady but not truly slow gallop on fast ground can set up a finisher who travels well in the slipstream and finds a clear run at the furlong marker, with Musselburgh's tight track rewarding horses that switch off early. Enemy Action and Claret And Blues are the truest hold-up types without redistribution concerns and both carry form figures suggesting placed ability on similar ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Lairy Mary goes too hard early even without pressure — perhaps due to a high draw or nervous debut energy — and ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A self-destructive pace from the leader creates a wall of closers hitting the line together, with midfield types getting the perfect tow before switching off the bridle. Stripes Of Glory and Bea Kindly would most benefit here, both capable of finishing through a gap if the front-runner fades sharply, though both carry style-fit discounts from redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Trouble Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If hold-up horses bunch in the closing stages and cause interference, promoting a mid-division tracker into an unexpected winning position.
scenarios.body: With four closers crammed into the rear half of only six runners, congestion at the two-furlong pole is plausible, particularly if Lairy Mary slows the pace enough that they all challenge simultaneously. Mr Darling, the lowest-rated and most lightly framed runner, would need this exact scenario — chaotic traffic that neutralises quality — to get involved, and even then his form figures make this the least likely winning outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Lairy Mary's early strides — if she breaks cleanly and immediately opens a gap, the race is effectively over as a tactical contest and front-running profiles will dominate from the first furlong.

Watch the hold-up cluster of Bea Kindly, Mr Darling, and Stripes Of Glory at the break — if two or more miss the kick and find themselves tangled together, traffic trouble in the final two furlongs becomes a genuine risk in this small-field sprint.

Watch Enemy Action's position after two furlongs — Harry Russell will need to slot it into a clear pocket rather than being buried on the rail, as a clean run is the single biggest determinant of whether its closing form can translate to a win here.

Watch the going confirmation at the track; the official description repeats as Good to Firm across all races, and if the ground is quicker than the race-day going states, Lairy Mary's ability to sustain her lead materially improves over the hold-up types who need loose ground to compensate for positional disadvantage.

races.name: Mr & Mrs McKinlay Wedding Anniversary Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up performer for Martin Todhunter who has a creditable placed run over 2 miles on good ground in his recent history (2nd/16f/GOO), though inconsistency at this trip is evident with a 12th from 16f on good last time; David Nolan takes over in the plate, the horse is unexposed under this jockey combination, and a patient ride from the rear is inevitable.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's seven-year-old was seen just eight days ago and has been notably consistent lately — a win and two thirds on soft and good ground at similar distances — giving him a strong going profile here; a natural hold-up performer, he will operate from the back and needs a pace scenario that sets up a staying finish rather than a tactical sprint.

runners_data.name: Lagoon Nebula
runners_data.note: Andrew Kinirons' five-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner, which at this venue and distance is a significant positional asset given the small field; recent form is mixed (9th, 2nd, 4th over comparable trips) but the ability to dictate unchallenged means energy expenditure can be minimised, and good-to-firm suits based on the going record.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears runs this six-year-old who has strong course-and-distance profile credentials — three wins and seven places over 12-17 furlong trips on good ground across 12 applicable runs — and the 5lb claimer Tom Kiely-Marshall offers a weight advantage; a natural prominent racer, he will likely sit just behind Lagoon Nebula and is well-placed for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' five-year-old has failed to win or place in his five most recent starts and has a modest going profile, showing no wins in ten runs on similar ground; his natural instinct is to race from the rear, but the congested back of this field means he is unlikely to find the space he needs, reducing the value of any late effort he might offer.

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's six-year-old has course-relevant credentials — a win over 16f on good ground and placed runs over 18f — and shapes as one of the leading prominent contenders alongside Max Of Stars; he will aim to track Lagoon Nebula closely through the early stages, and his recent form line of 3-4-0-0-5 includes a fifth after a break, so fitness is a mild consideration after 21 days off.

runners_data.name: Speechman
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's six-year-old carries both a "fades in finish" warning and a redistributed tag, meaning he is a genuine hold-up type whose form has regressed sharply (8th, 8th, 9th) and who is unlikely to reproduce earlier placed efforts (2nd, 3rd) in his current state; the STYLE_FIT concern compounds a weak recent record, and at OR 48 he faces stiff tasks against better-handicapped rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Lagoon Nebula is the lone confirmed front-runner and, over 2 miles on good-to-firm ground at Musselburgh with just seven runners, faces no meaningful pressure for the early lead — they will control the pace from the front and set a comfortable, sustainable gallop that is unlikely to be excessive. Newport and Max Of Stars are the natural prominent types who will track close behind, forming a small group near the head of affairs while Arrange, Cascade Hall, Speechman, and Mr Withington operate further back. The field does contain more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Speechman and Mr Withington are genuine hold-up performers mapped to midfield because the back of the field is congested, meaning they are unlikely to reproduce their natural closing run from as far back as they would ideally want. At 2 miles with an uncontested front-runner dictating a measured tempo, this race shape clearly favours prominent racers with proven form at the trip and going, who can travel efficiently behind Lagoon Nebula and pounce before true hold-up closers can wind up from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lagoon Nebula Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent trackers travel smoothly in behind.
scenarios.body: Lagoon Nebula dictates a steady pace through the middle stages and the race becomes a test of tactical efficiency rather than raw stamina, with Newport and Max Of Stars ideally placed to challenge as the tempo lifts entering the straight; horses racing prominently at Musselburgh over 2 miles on good-to-firm ground historically hold a decisive positional edge when the pace has been unhurried.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the sprint home is compressed, allowing a true finisher to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Cascade Hall, who has placed consistently at this sort of distance and is freshened up after just 8 days (having run well recently), would be the most credible closer given form figures of 1-3-4 over staying trips on similar ground; Arrange has shown placed form over 2 miles on good ground before and could benefit if the race becomes a late dash, though both face the challenge of making up ground on a field that won't have been burned up early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Lagoon Nebula Leads Home
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula's controlled front-running is simply too difficult to peg back and no rival has the gears to close in the straight.
scenarios.body: A sustainable tempo ridden by a horse who knows its job can translate to a winning performance, particularly on good-to-firm ground where front-runners who save energy in the early stages can find a second wind; Lagoon Nebula's recent form shows a second and a fourth at comparable distances, and racing from a familiar prominent position at a venue where pace tactics matter means the role itself suits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Withington or Speechman somehow secure a better position than expected and the pace is genuinely sedate, flattering their finishing effort.
scenarios.body: Both horses are flagged as genuine hold-up types forced into a midfield role by race shape rather than choice, and both carry STYLE_FIT tags indicating they are out of their natural running role, which limits their expected contribution significantly; Speechman in particular carries a fades-in-finish flag and has produced several poor recent runs, making this the least likely shape to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Newport and Max Of Stars will contest the second and third positions early — if either pushes forward aggressively to sit closer to Lagoon Nebula than expected, watch for a miniature pace battle developing which could lift the tempo and compromise the front-runner's advantage.

Cascade Hall returned just eight days ago and runs again quickly here — watch whether Jim Goldie's horse travels smoothly in the first half of the race; any sign of laboured movement before the straight would suggest the quick turnaround has taken a toll.

Speechman's "fades in finish" flag combined with a string of poor recent runs means punters holding each-way interest in this horse should watch early whether any energy is wasted trying to find a better position than the race shape naturally affords.

On good-to-firm ground at Musselburgh over 2 miles the pace is unlikely to be truly searching — watch the split time at the 1-mile marker to judge whether Lagoon Nebula is conserving enough energy that a late rattle from Cascade Hall or Arrange becomes viable, or whether the race effectively concludes turning for home.

races.name: Celebrating The Musselburgh Festival 2026 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who handles good ground well (2/7f/GOO in latest, 0W4P at the trip on similar going) and is capable of hitting the frame, though needs a strong pace to close into — Katie Scott's yard returns 1/13 over 14 days so timing could be sharper.

runners_data.name: Carolus Magnus
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who won over this course and distance last time (1/7f/GOO), is effective from a prominent position, and benefits from Joanna Mason's local knowledge; his record of 2W4P on similar going makes him a consistent threat from just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: In-form sprinter who has won three of his last five on comparable going, but his natural prominent style is squeezed out in this field — he will likely race further back than ideal, and that positional compromise tempers what his form figures suggest.

runners_data.name: Supreme Clarets
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old who has placed twice on good ground at 7f and is handled by the powerful Fahey operation (4/44 in 14 days); holds-up in midfield and needs a genuine gallop to bring his finishing effort to bear.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Won three of his last five starts including twice on good ground over 7f, and his prominent racing style is perfectly aligned with what this race shape rewards; Iain Jardine in good 14-day form (5/29) adds trainer confidence to a horse already well-suited by the conditions.

runners_data.name: We've Got This
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners a genuine hold-up horse who has been placed on good ground but is mapped into midfield because true rear-of-field positioning is already occupied — racing somewhat out of role, and that positional friction will need to be overcome before any finishing burst can land.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old is a confirmed hold-up specialist with only one place from seven runs on good ground at 7f (0W1P), and his redistributed midfield position compounds the challenge of a race shape that will likely be resolved well before he gets rolling.

runners_data.name: Lady Gormire
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and the horse who sets the entire race template; Michael Dods's three-year-old has placed four times from five runs on good ground and simply needs to find the line quickly once her uncontested lead is established.

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's progressive three-year-old races prominently and has a win and two placings on good ground; dropped to 7f from a mile and a half campaign, the shorter trip will test his pace but his profile suits racing close to a sustainable pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old won at 8f on good ground but has dropped to 7f and posted a zero latest — prominent in style, and if he bounces back the trip and ground are not obvious barriers, though the 0 last time must be respected.

runners_data.name: No Return
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old is a hold-up horse whose recent form is full of minor placings at 6f on good ground; stepping up to 7f and drawn in a field where the pace will be controlled, he needs the leaders to come back to him — which may not happen at this tempo.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Gormire is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f handicap and, crucially, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — she should stride into a comfortable, rhythm-dictating position from the first furlong on good-to-firm ground. Behind her, Carolus Magnus, The Gay Blade, Masaban, and Napolian form a cluster of genuine prominent types who will contest the chasing positions, creating a race run at a fair but controlled tempo that is unlikely to be truly punishing early. The field contains more pace-seeking types than the shape can accommodate: Keep Me Stable is a natural prominent racer who will likely find himself racing further back than ideal, while We've Got This and Yaaser are true hold-up horses pushed into a mapped midfield position that does not reflect their natural style. This race shape — a sustainable, uncontested gallop set by one front-runner with a competitive prominent group in attendance — most strongly favours front-running and prominent types who can sit close to Lady Gormire, travel comfortably, and produce their effort from two furlongs out rather than launching from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Gormire Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Gormire bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair, even gallop that suits those close to the pace.
scenarios.body: Lady Gormire dictates from the front, the race unfolds at a sustainable clip that allows the prominent group to track without over-exertion, and the winner comes from the first four or five positions as the finish line approaches.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Overwhelms
scenarios.trigger: If Carolus Magnus or The Gay Blade push aggressively early and the pace quickens, applying pressure to Lady Gormire from the second furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuinely competitive gallop develops between Lady Gormire and the chasing prominent horses, and the race resolves in favour of the horse with the best combination of stamina and tactical position rounding the final bend.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hot enough to unwind the front-runners and a midfield stalker finds clear running inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Supreme Clarets or Black Storm, racing in an honest midfield, benefit if the leaders tie themselves up and the closing kick from a well-positioned midfield horse gets the race verdict.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses those close to it and genuine hold-up horses get a clean run through beaten rivals late.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires We've Got This or Yaaser to navigate traffic and produce a finishing burst they are not naturally well-placed to deliver given their redistributed map positions, making it the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Lady Gormire's ability to control tempo entirely unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaper — watch the first two furlongs to see if Carolus Magnus or The Gay Blade push up aggressively and compromise her rhythm.

The Gay Blade's price could be affected by his trainer's excellent 14-day strike rate (5/29) and three wins in his last five outings — horses with this profile can be underestimated in handicap company when form and stable confidence align.

Keep Me Stable's true prominent style being squeezed to a midfield role is a structural disadvantage — watch whether David Allan attempts to push forward early regardless, which would inject unexpected early pace and reshape the scenario probabilities.

Supreme Clarets has placed twice on good at 7f for the Fahey yard and represents a consistent each-way profile for a race where the midfield finishing lane could be competitive if the pace is strong enough to unwind the prominent group.

Napolian's blank (0) last time at 8f on good may represent a misleading piece of form given the step back to 7f suits his style — monitor market support as a guide to whether David O'Meara's yard expects a bounce.

races.name: Hays Travel Holiday Outside The Box Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 12-13f on good ground (four seconds in last six runs), genuine hold-up type who has been pushed into a midfield map position — in practice will settle at the rear and need a strong pace to maximise her finishing effort, which this race may not provide.

runners_data.name: Fleur de Mer
runners_data.note: Lightly raced on similar going (2/15 sim-going, 0W0P), handles soft better than fast conditions; naturally races from hold-up and is bumped into a midfield mapping here because the field is overloaded with rear-runners — the quick surface is a concern and her recent form shows no wins in this grade.

runners_data.name: Forever Perfect
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with consistent placed form over 12f at Southwell on standard, now stepping into good-to-firm for the first time in recent runs — has won over 12f and the trip extension to 14½f looks positive; a genuine closer who should appreciate any finishing kick off whatever pace Max Of Stars sets.

runners_data.name: Hansteen
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a course win over 12f on good and placed again at the same track — John & Sean Quinn yard in fair form (T14: 2/10) and Jason Hart takes the ride; naturally a hold-up runner but compact enough in profile to travel closer than his mapped position suggests, making him one of the more interesting tactical options if he can attach to Max Of Stars.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears's six-year-old is the lone front-runner, boasts excellent sim-going form (12/15, 3W7P) and has winning course form over 16f — the drop back to 14½f suits, the 5lb claimer adds risk but uncontested lead on a flat, right-handed galloping track is his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: In poor recent form (no wins in last 10, consistently mid-to-rear finisher on various going), Ewan Whillans's five-year-old is a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map — 135lbs is the joint-heaviest burden among the redistributed group, and the quick ground doesn't obviously suit his profile.

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner dropping back from 8-10f trips where she has struggled (7/15 sim-going, seven of last nine in bottom half of field) — the step up to 14½f looks an experiment rather than a solution, and hold-up style at a distance she hasn't previously tested is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen on board for Iain Jardine, who is firing (T14: 5/29); the eight-year-old has placed form over 16f on good ground (2nd, 3rd) and genuinely handles this trip — a true staying closer who needs the race to be run at a proper gallop to reel in Max Of Stars.

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a solid record of placed form at 10-12f on good (three thirds and a win in last nine), naturally races from hold-up but has consistent finishing form — R Mike Smith's runner carries 133lbs and the sim-going record (9/15, 1W7P) suggests she is competitive without being a dominant force.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — Jim Goldie's four-year-old has not won or placed in any recent run on good ground (7/10 sim-going, 0W0P) and the redistribution into midfield map from hold-up is academic given the finishing concerns; hard to construct a winning scenario.

runners_data.name: Talking In Kode
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old (T14: 7/32, in very good form) has been campaigned over shorter trips (8-10f) and this 14½f represents a significant step up in trip — Cian Horgan (5lb) in the saddle, naturally a hold-up type mapped mid-field; strong trainer form is the angle but the distance is unproven.

runners_data.name: Time Twister
runners_data.note: 292 days off the track is the dominant concern — Michael & David Easterby's three-year-old returns from a lengthy absence with a form string showing no placed run on good ground in recent outings; Joanna Mason rides but ring-rustiness over an unfamiliar trip makes this very hard to assess with confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Max Of Stars is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 1m4½f handicap and, critically, faces no genuine pace pressure — with every other runner in the field carrying a hold-up profile, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on good-to-firm ground. The true pace shape here is extremely thin at the head of affairs: Fleur de Mer, Talking In Kode, Mr Withington and others are naturally prominent or hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because this field simply cannot accommodate them all at the rear, but none are likely to challenge Max Of Stars for the lead. With one horse setting an uncontested tempo over a galloping track at Musselburgh and the surface riding quick, this race shape strongly favours Max Of Stars himself to control the pace and, critically, horses with proven come-from-behind ability in similar conditions — but the absence of genuine pace pressure means a true late-run scenario is weakened, and horses that can travel prominently behind the leader and quicken off a modest gallop hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Max Of Stars Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Max Of Stars has strong course-and-distance form, handles good-to-firm well (12/15 sim-going runs) and has won over 16f on this track — bowling along solo on a flat, galloping course is his ideal scenario, and with no pace rival to push him wide or hollow him out, he can conserve energy before kicking clear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars sets an overly slow pace that compresses the field, allowing genuine closers to produce a finishing burst in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian early gallop paradoxically helps horses like Ravenscraig Castle and Forever Perfect, who have consistent placed form at 12-16f in similar conditions and can motor home when the pace quickens late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed midfield types — most likely Hansteen or Talking In Kode — manages to track Max Of Stars closely and outstays him in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Hansteen has course-winning form over 12f in similar going and, despite being mapped to midfield due to overcrowding, has the tactical speed and youth (age 3) to sit just off the leader's shoulder; if Max Of Stars ties up, a prominent tracker benefits most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars is withdrawn, stumbles, or the field fragments completely with multiple horses attempting to take up a forward position.
scenarios.body: Without a reliable pacemaker, the race degenerates into a messy, uneven gallop that could produce a shock result from an unconsidered hold-up performer making late ground.

watchPoints.text: Max Of Stars (sole pace-setter) — watch whether Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) allows him to bowl along comfortably or gets crowded at the start; if he misses the break, the entire pace dynamic collapses.

Ravenscraig Castle — Andrew Mullen and a trainer in form (5/29 T14) make him the most credible challenger; watch his position rounding the final bend — if he is within three lengths of Max Of Stars at the two-furlong pole, he is a live danger.

Hansteen — three-year-old with proven course form who could travel closer than his mapped position suggests; if Jason Hart elects to push him up behind the leader early rather than dropping in, the race shape changes significantly.

Time Twister — 292-day layoff means she is effectively an unknown quantity on return; watch her market drift or firm in the morning, as significant money for a horse resuming from this long a break would be a strong stable signal.

Talking In Kode — Edward Bethell's excellent recent strike rate (7/32 T14) means this runner should not be dismissed despite the unproven trip; watch whether she travels with any fluency in mid-division, as a horse stepping markedly up in distance who travels sweetly is typically a positive sign.

races.name: Edinburgh Childrens Hospital Charity Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 8yo has strong good-ground form at 5f (2nd last run) and arrives fit on 6 days' rest, but his true style is a hold-up closer who will likely find himself deeper in the pack than ideal in this pace-compressed field — his finishing kick is genuine but he needs room.|

runners_data.name: Hard Nut
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 9yo returns on 21 days off with a poor recent record (9th, 7th, 7th last three) and has placed only once from seven similar-going starts; though a natural closer, his age and form make him the weakest of the Perratt trio.|

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: The best-performed of Perratt's three runners here with a win and two places over 5f on similar ground; a natural hold-up type who has been squeezed into the midfield pack and will need a gap to appear at the right moment rather than getting his cleanest run.|

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Gary Harrison's 4yo carries top weight and has placed three times on good ground over 5f including a recent third; ridden by Barry McHugh, he comes from hold-up positions and posted a win from the front last season, suggesting he can adapt if traffic thins.|

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' 4yo brings a win and a place from six recent starts on good ground and arrives fresh on 8 days; a hold-up operator by profile, he has posted prominent-looking sectionals recently and could be the one closers' representative who actually gets a decent pitch mid-race.|

runners_data.name: Keldeo
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' 5yo is the key pace-setter here — two wins and four places on good ground from 10 starts is an outstanding record for this surface, and a 35-day break after a run of consistent fourth-place efforts suggests a stable happy to wait for the right spot; the [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects that this shape is moderately busier than ideal but he is still the lone confirmed leader.|

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4yo has won twice on good ground at 5f (1W2P from nine similar-going runs) and arrives on 16 days' rest in good nick; a genuine hold-up type in natural role here, he has the finishing acceleration to be dangerous if the pace is strong enough to string things out.|

runners_data.name: Peregrine Falcon
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris's 4yo returns after 47 days — the longest break in this field — with all five recent runs at Southwell on standard, making his turf form profile genuinely uncertain; a natural closer whose going stats here (0W1P from four) are modest, and the layoff adds to the risk.|

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 8yo has five good-ground 5f starts with zero wins and four places — consistent but limited; his true hold-up style has been redistributed into a midfield slot, and while he plugs on reliably, a race run at controlled pace without a strong closing burst blunts his main weapon.|

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan's 5yo is a standout on recent form — 3W8P from 13 good-ground starts including three second-place finishes in the last five — and arrives fresh on 8 days under a top jockey; the prominent style suits this shape perfectly as the natural stalker of Keldeo, and Jim Goldie's 5/65 strike-rate over 14 days suggests the stable is in form.|

races.paceDynamic: Keldeo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 5f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Musselburgh, and with no genuine rival to push him from the gates he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a scorching early tempo. Woohoo is the one prominent type who will press forward alongside or just behind Keldeo, meaning the pace is real enough to string the field out but not so fierce that the leader ties up. The bulk of the field — Albegone, Henery Hawk, Peregrine Falcon, Sixcor and others — are natural hold-up horses who have been pushed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many genuine closers for the rear to accommodate them all; the horses most likely to actually secure prominent ground behind Keldeo are Woohoo and, at a stretch, Jm Jhingree given his recent front-placed effort. A controlled lone-leader scenario on a flat, fast track favours prominent racers who can track the pace and pounce without the need for a strong finish to develop — hold-up horses facing a compressed midfield will be in traffic trouble and need things to go their way.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keldeo Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo dictates an uncontested moderate gallop and the race is decided by those closest to the pace turning in.
scenarios.body: Keldeo bowls along on the stands rail setting a fractions-controlled tempo, with Woohoo tracking him in second and a gap back to the congested midfield; rounding the home turn those two are best placed and the race becomes a sprint-from-the-front duel.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves fast enough to set up a pronounced closing burst in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Should Woohoo push the early splits harder than ideal, or if Keldeo goes off quick from the gates, the pace quickens enough that the genuine hold-up types finishing from off the pace — Albegone and Marajito — arrive with room to fly late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early pace causes bunching and several midfield runners arrive upsides in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: A crawl in the early stages compresses the field into a wall of horses at the two-furlong marker, effectively making this a sprint from the turn; horses with a sharp turn of foot in a messy finish like Sixcor and Henery Hawk could thread through, though both are racing out of their natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo is allowed to ping the gate and build an unassailable lead that never gets pegged back.
scenarios.body: On a flat, fast Musselburgh 5f with no challenger pressing and a comfortable weight advantage, Keldeo simply slips the field from the off and the hold-up horses can never close the gap from their compromised midfield berths.

watchPoints.text: Woohoo and Keldeo — watch how quickly they establish positions at the gates; if Mulrennan sends Woohoo forward to sit on Keldeo's shoulder from the off, the race is effectively run between those two throughout.|

Albegone and Marajito — both Tim Easterby hold-up horses in the same race could box each other in; watch how the draw and early positioning affects which one gets the cleaner passage in the closing stages.|

Peregrine Falcon — 47 days off and an all-Southwell recent form profile means this horse's turf readiness is genuinely unclear; if it shows any greenness or traffic hesitation early it is out of the race before the turn.|

The midfield cluster (Henery Hawk, Sixcor, Hard Nut, Jm Jhingree) — with four horses competing for the same late-running space and all shuffled closer together than their natural positions, monitor the draw and early stall exits for which one avoids getting boxed behind the prominent pair.|

races.name: Lucas Ice Cream Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two wins at a mile on good ground (sim-going 2W3P from 8 runs) and a tenacious front-run at Goodwood on most recent start; however the field's hold-up concentration means this horse will likely be shuffled into a position further forward than ideal, racing out of its natural late-running role.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has failed to win in 15 starts on similar going (0W0P) and whose recent form figures of 6-6-6-8-5 offer nothing to encourage; the step to a mile-and-a-furlong does not obviously help a horse yet to find the front at this level.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing six-year-old who has finished second twice in similar going and handles Musselburgh's flat straight well; Cian Horgan's claim brings the weight down and tracking Positive Thoughts from a handy early position is exactly the tactical brief this horse needs.

runners_data.name: Samra Star
runners_data.note: Jockey booking is unconfirmed in the data but this five-year-old's natural style is to come from well off the pace — a tactic that the race's modest single-pace-setter makes difficult — and with only 1 place from 2 similar-going runs the form on this surface is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Hold-up four-year-old flagged as a fader in the finish, which is a meaningful concern in a race where the end-to-end gallop is likely to be moderate and the final two furlongs will favour horses with a sharp turn of foot rather than sustained stayers who idle.

runners_data.name: War Memorial
runners_data.note: Won twice at seven furlongs on good ground and clearly best at that trip; the step up to a mile-and-a-furlong looks a stretch for a horse that has been placed only four times from 15 similar-going starts, and only an 8-day turnaround means freshness is not a concern though fitness after a short break at this longer trip is.

runners_data.name: Pebble Dash
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated horse in the field (OR 45) whose form string of 4-4-4-4-0 maps a consistent also-ran pattern; Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim helps, but this is a true deep-hold-up type whose chance depends on a pace strength this race will not provide.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old has the strongest similar-going profile in the field (sim-going 2W9P from 12 runs, OR 59) and has been placed at a mile on good ground twice recently; prominent racing style means she can sit just behind Positive Thoughts and strike when it matters, and the Easterby yard is operating at a productive 9/72 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner who will command the lead uncontested and set a pace entirely of his own choosing; John & Sean Quinn have had two winners from ten runners in the last fortnight, and while this horse has finished no higher than third in recent starts on similar ground, the ability to dictate terms without pressure is a major tactical asset today.

races.paceDynamic: Positive Thoughts is the sole confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will be allowed to stride clear from the gates and dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this flat Musselburgh mile-and-a-furlong on good-to-firm ground. Book Of Life and Perfidia are the two prominent types best placed to track the pace closely, and with Positive Thoughts setting a sustainable rather than scorching tempo, the race is likely to develop as a straightforward test of stamina-tinged class rather than a speed duel. The field carries a heavy concentration of hold-up horses — Approaching Dawn, Samra Star, and Pebble Dash are all true come-from-behind types redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; War Memorial and Toy Soldier add further hold-up weight, meaning those needing cover will be queuing for the same ground in the straight. This shape clearly favours horses racing prominently or making sustained progress from the front third, with true hold-up horses dependent on a strong pace they are unlikely to get.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Positive Thoughts Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts bowls along uncontested and sets a fair, rhythmic gallop that suits those tracking the pace.
scenarios.body: Positive Thoughts dictates from the front and never faces a serious challenge to its position, with Perfidia and Book Of Life the closest pursuers capitalising on the untroubled tempo. A race run at this shape rewards prominent, travelling types who can quicken off a moderate pace in the straight, and the front three market positions are filled from within that group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Perfidia or Book Of Life travel powerfully into the straight and collared Positive Thoughts as the pace eases in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Positive Thoughts has done the donkey work setting the pace and is picked off close home by one or both of the prominent trackers who have conserved energy whilst holding a winning position throughout. Perfidia's strong course and distance form on similar going makes her the principal beneficiary, with Book Of Life's second at a mile on good ground also relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: War Memorial Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If War Memorial is ridden handily enough and the pace slackens sufficiently to allow a powerful late run from the rear of the midfield group.
scenarios.body: War Memorial's form figures of 1-1-3 at seven furlongs on good ground show a sharp, tactical horse who has proven ability to quicken, and if the field concertinas in the straight he could thread through late. Two wins and three places from four similar-going runs suggests the horse retains ability, though dropping back from seven furlongs to a mile-and-a-furlong on this occasion is a significant step up in trip that may blunt the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely quickens early and strings the field out, creating a true test that allows the deep hold-up horses to close ground in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a genuinely strong early gallop that the single front-runner profile makes unlikely, and the horses best placed to benefit — Approaching Dawn, Samra Star, Pebble Dash — are all redistributed true hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural position in this compressed field. Even if one lands a blow, the structural disadvantage of being a genuine closer in a race with a single steady pace-setter makes this the least probable shape to reward.

watchPoints.text: Perfidia — if she travels smoothly in second or third on the rail behind Positive Thoughts turning for home, her superior similar-going record (2W9P from 12 runs) makes her a serious threat to lead close home.

Positive Thoughts — watch the early exchanges to see whether the pace is genuinely modest; if the horse idles and shortens stride on the straight, Book Of Life and Perfidia are both positioned to pounce.

War Memorial — drops back in trip from seven furlongs to a mile-and-a-furlong and has only 8 days between runs; if the horse travels freely early and rider positions up handy rather than holding up, the class is there for a bold show.

Approaching Dawn, Samra Star, Pebble Dash — all three are natural hold-up types competing for the same late-running ground; if they crowd each other in the straight or find themselves without a clear run, their individual chances are significantly diminished by the race shape.

Toy Soldier — the "fades in finish" flag combined with the hold-up style is a particular concern at a mile-and-a-furlong on good-to-firm, where the absence of a strong pace means the horse may idle in the straight without the cover it needs to produce its best.
